0: How many books are there in the Torah?
Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy: it is also called the Pentateuch.
1: According to Genesis, who built an ark to survive the flood?
He brought his family and animals of every kind on board (Genesis 6–9).
2: What is the first book of the Torah?
In Hebrew it is called Bereshit, “In the beginning”.
3: In the Torah, what is the name of Abraham’s wife, the mother of Isaac?
According to Genesis, she had Isaac at a very old age (Genesis 21).
4: According to Genesis, in which garden did Adam and Eve live?
It is also called the earthly Paradise (Genesis 2).
5: What new name did Jacob receive after wrestling all night long?
This name is the origin of the expression “children of Israel” (Genesis 32).
6: How many sons did Jacob have?
They are the ancestors of the 12 tribes of Israel (Genesis 35).
7: What is the name of Jacob’s twin brother?
He sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of lentil stew (Genesis 25).
8: In the Torah, who is Isaac’s wife?
Abraham’s servant met her near a well (Genesis 24).
9: From which city did Abraham set out with his father Terah?
Ur was in Mesopotamia, in present-day Iraq (Genesis 11).
10: Which cave did Abraham buy in Hebron to bury Sarah?
According to tradition, the patriarchs and their wives are buried there (Genesis 23).
11: According to Jewish tradition, how many commandments (mitzvot) are there in the Torah?
Tradition divides them into 248 positive commandments and 365 prohibitions.
12: What did Moses’ mother place him in on the Nile?
A basket of reeds coated with tar, hidden among the bulrushes (Exodus 2).
13: According to the Torah, how many plagues struck Egypt?
The last one was the death of the firstborn (Exodus 7–12).
14: On which mountain did Moses receive the Tablets of the Law?
According to Exodus, Moses stayed there 40 days and 40 nights (Exodus 24).
15: Which sea parted to let the Hebrews cross?
In Hebrew it is called Yam Suf, the “Sea of Reeds” (Exodus 14).
16: How many commandments were engraved on the Tablets of the Law?
They are also called the Decalogue (Exodus 20).
17: Who was Moses’ brother, who became the first high priest?
He often spoke for Moses before Pharaoh (Exodus 4).
18: What food fell from the sky to feed the Hebrews in the desert?
It fell every morning, except on Shabbat (Exodus 16).
19: For how many years did the Hebrews wander in the desert?
According to the Torah, a whole generation passed before they entered Canaan (Numbers 14).
20: What idol did the Hebrews make while Moses was on the mountain?
When he saw it, Moses broke the first Tablets of the Law (Exodus 32).
21: What is the name of Moses’ father-in-law, a priest of Midian?
He advised Moses to appoint judges to help him (Exodus 18).
22: Which sister of Moses sang with a tambourine after crossing the sea?
23: Who succeeded Moses in leading the people into Canaan?
The fall of the walls of Jericho is linked to him (Joshua 6).
24: Which young shepherd defeated the giant Goliath with a sling?
He later became king of Israel (1 Samuel 17).
25: Which king of Israel is famous for his great wisdom?
The son of David, he built the First Temple in Jerusalem (1 Kings 3 and 6).
26: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish?
He spent 3 days and 3 nights in the belly of the fish (Jonah 2).
27: Which biblical hero drew his strength from his hair?
He lost his strength when Delilah had his hair cut (Judges 16).
28: What kind of den was the prophet Daniel thrown into?
According to the Book of Daniel, the lions did him no harm (Daniel 6).
29: Who was the first king of Israel?
He was anointed by the prophet Samuel (1 Samuel 10).
30: What instrument did David play to calm King Saul?
The Hebrew instrument, the kinnor, is also translated as “lyre” (1 Samuel 16).
31: Which prophet was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire?
His disciple Elisha witnessed the scene (2 Kings 2).
32: Which woman was both a judge and a prophetess of Israel?
She judged the people under a palm tree (Judges 4).
33: Which prophet anointed the young David to become king?
David was the youngest of Jesse’s sons (1 Samuel 16).
34: Which people did Ruth, King David’s great-grandmother, belong to?
She told her mother-in-law Naomi: “Your people shall be my people” (Ruth 1).
35: Which queen visited King Solomon to test his wisdom?
She brought him gold, spices and precious stones (1 Kings 10).
36: Which Jewish holiday commemorates the Exodus from Egypt?
It lasts 7 or 8 days depending on where you live.
37: How many days does Hanukkah last?
One more candle is lit each evening on a special candelabrum, the hanukkiah.
38: What unleavened bread is eaten during Passover?
According to Exodus, the Hebrews left so quickly that their dough had no time to rise (Exodus 12).
39: During which Jewish holiday do children dress up in costumes?
People read the Megillah, give gifts of food and give to the poor.
40: What is the Jewish New Year called?
Traditionally, people eat an apple dipped in honey to wish for a sweet year.
41: Which fast day is called the “Day of Atonement”?
It is the most solemn day of the Jewish year, with a fast of about 25 hours.
42: During which holiday are meals eaten in a hut?
The hut, the sukkah, recalls the shelters of the Hebrews in the desert (Leviticus 23).
43: What is the name of the horn blown on Rosh Hashanah?
It is most often made from a ram’s horn.
44: Which queen is the heroine of Purim?
According to the Book of Esther, she saved the Jews of Persia from a plot.
45: What does the holiday of Shavuot commemorate?
It falls 7 weeks after Passover; Shavuot means “weeks”.
46: After the victory of the Maccabees in the 2nd century BCE; according to tradition, a small jar of oil burned for 8 days.
47: What is the ritual meal on the first night of Passover called?
The Haggadah, the story of the Exodus from Egypt, is read during it.
48: It lasts from sunset on Friday until nightfall on Saturday.
49: What is the Jewish place of prayer called?
The word comes from Greek and means “assembly”.
50: What is the small cap worn on the head called?
It is worn as a sign of respect for God.
51: In which language was the Torah written?
Hebrew is written from right to left.
52: What is the 7-branched candelabrum of the Temple called?
How it was made is described in the Torah (Exodus 25).
53: What is inside the mezuzah fixed to doorposts?
The verses from Deuteronomy are handwritten by a scribe (Deuteronomy 6).
54: What are the Jewish dietary laws called?
Food that follows these rules is called “kosher”.
55: What is the fringed prayer shawl called?
Its fringes, the tzitzit, are commanded in the Torah (Numbers 15).
56: Which ceremony marks a boy’s religious coming of age at 13?
For girls, it is the bat mitzvah, usually at 12.
57: How many letters are there in the Hebrew alphabet?
All of them are consonants; 5 letters have a special form at the end of a word.
58: Which prayer begins with “Hear, O Israel”?
Its opening words come from Deuteronomy (Deuteronomy 6:4).
59: What is the ceremony that marks the end of Shabbat called?
It uses wine, fragrant spices and a braided candle.
60: In which city stood the Temple of ancient Israel?
The First Temple was built under King Solomon.
61: Which ancient people destroyed the Second Temple in Jerusalem in the year 70?
The city was taken by the troops of the general Titus.
62: What is the remaining part of the Temple’s outer wall in Jerusalem, where people pray, called?
In Hebrew it is called the Kotel, “the wall”; it is also known as the Wailing Wall.
63: What is the genocide of the Jews during the Second World War called?
About 6 million Jews were murdered by the Nazi regime; it is also called the Holocaust.
64: Which Jewish girl wrote a famous diary while hiding in Amsterdam?
Her diary, published after the war by her father, has been translated into dozens of languages.
65: Which king of Babylon destroyed the First Temple in Jerusalem?
This was in 587 or 586 BCE; part of the people was exiled to Babylon.
66: Which Persian king allowed the Jewish exiles to return to Jerusalem?
According to the Book of Ezra, he also allowed the Temple to be rebuilt (Ezra 1).
67: Which language of the Jews of Central and Eastern Europe mixes German and Hebrew?
Yiddish is written with the Hebrew alphabet.
68: What are Jews whose ancestors lived in Spain and Portugal called?
The word comes from Sepharad, the Hebrew name for the Iberian Peninsula.
69: In which Andalusian city was the scholar Maimonides born?
Born in the 12th century, a philosopher and physician, he wrote the “Guide for the Perplexed”.
70: In which French city did Rashi, the famous commentator on the Bible and the Talmud, live?
Born in 1040, he is the most studied commentator in Jewish tradition.
71: In which year were the Jews expelled from Spain?
The expulsion decree was signed by the Catholic Monarchs; many left for Morocco and the Ottoman Empire.
72: According to Genesis, in how many days did God create the world before resting?
The 7th day, God’s day of rest, is the origin of Shabbat.
73: According to Genesis, from which part of Adam’s body was Eve created?
Adam had fallen into a deep sleep while God formed her.
74: According to Genesis, what sign did God place in the sky after the flood?
It symbolises the promise never again to destroy the earth by a flood.
75: According to Genesis, which favourite son of Jacob was given a coat of many colours?
Out of jealousy, his brothers sold him as a slave to merchants travelling to Egypt.
76: According to Genesis, what did Jacob see in a dream, with angels going up and down it?
When he woke up, he named the place Bethel, “house of God”.
77: According to Genesis, which animal did Abraham sacrifice in place of Isaac?
The animal was caught by its horns in a thicket on Mount Moriah.
78: According to Genesis, which woman was turned into a pillar of salt while fleeing Sodom?
She had looked back at the city being destroyed, even though it was forbidden.
79: For which woman did Jacob work 14 years for his uncle Laban?
Laban first tricked him into marrying his elder daughter, Leah.
80: According to Genesis, what did the 7 fat cows in Pharaoh’s dream stand for?
The 7 thin cows foretold 7 years of famine that would follow.
81: What is the last book of the Torah?
It ends with the death of Moses, on the threshold of the Promised Land.
82: According to Genesis, what was the name of Sarah’s Egyptian maidservant, the mother of Ishmael?
Her son Ishmael was Abraham’s firstborn.
83: What was the name of the daughter of Jacob and Leah?
She is the only daughter of Jacob whose birth is described in Genesis.
84: According to Genesis, how old was Abraham when Isaac was born?
Sarah was 90, which made her laugh when this birth was announced.
85: According to the Torah, in what form did God appear to Moses in the desert?
The bush was on fire but was not burnt up.
86: In which country were the Hebrews slaves before the Exodus?
87: According to the Torah, what was the first plague of Egypt?
The water of the Nile became blood and the fish died.
88: According to the Torah, who found baby Moses on the bank of the Nile?
She is said to have given him the name Moses, “drawn out of the water”.
89: According to the Torah, what object did Moses hold to perform wonders?
According to the story, this staff turned into a snake in front of Pharaoh.
90: According to the Torah, what was the tenth and final plague of Egypt?
The Hebrews were spared by marking their doors with the blood of a lamb.
91: In which sacred chest were the Tablets of the Law kept?
It was covered in gold and topped with 2 cherubim.
92: What was the portable sanctuary the Hebrews carried through the desert called?
It was taken down and put back up at every stage of the journey.
93: How many spies did Moses send to explore the land of Canaan?
One per tribe; they brought back a huge cluster of grapes.
94: According to the Torah, which birds did God send to feed the Hebrews in the desert?
They arrived in the evening and covered the camp.
95: According to the Torah, what was the name of Moses’ wife?
She was one of the 7 daughters of a priest of Midian.
96: According to the Torah, on which mountain did Moses die after seeing the Promised Land?
This mountain is in present-day Jordan.
97: Which people attacked the Hebrews at Rephidim while Moses kept his arms raised?
Aaron and Hur held up Moses’ arms so that he could keep them raised.
98: According to the Bible, which city’s walls came tumbling down at the sound of trumpets?
The Hebrews had marched around it for 7 days.
99: According to the Book of Judges, which woman handed a hero over to his enemies after discovering the secret of his strength?
She was paid by the enemy leaders to find out this secret.
100: Which book of the Hebrew Bible is a collection of 150 songs and prayers?
In Hebrew it is called Tehillim, “praises”.
101: According to the Bible, which righteous man lost all his possessions and his children but kept his faith?
His name has become a byword for patience in hard times.
102: According to the Bible, which people did the giant Goliath belong to?
The Bible says he was more than 6 cubits tall.
103: According to the Book of Judges, which judge defeated the Midianites with only 300 men?
His men surprised the enemy at night with trumpets and torches hidden in jars.
104: To which great Assyrian city was the prophet who was swallowed by a great fish sent?
According to the story, the people repented and the city was spared.
105: According to the Bible, which queen, wife of King Ahab, persecuted the prophets?
She was a Phoenician princess, the daughter of the king of Sidon.
106: After the kingdom split in two, what was the southern kingdom, with Jerusalem as its capital, called?
The word “Jew” comes from the name Judah.
107: Which book of the Bible gathers sayings such as “Pride goes before a fall”?
Jewish tradition attributes most of it to a king famous for his wisdom.
108: Which prophet, the author of Lamentations according to tradition, witnessed the destruction of the First Temple?
He had long foretold the fall of Jerusalem, but no one listened.
109: Which prophet had a vision of a valley of dry bones coming back to life?
He prophesied during the exile of the people of Judah in Babylon.
110: Which king of Judah had a tunnel dug to bring spring water into Jerusalem?
This tunnel, about 500 metres long, still exists today.
111: What is the 9-branched candelabrum lit during Hanukkah called?
The 9th branch holds the shamash, the candle used to light the others.
112: What game do children traditionally play at Hanukkah?
Each of its 4 sides bears a Hebrew letter.
113: At the Jewish New Year, what are pieces of apple dipped in to wish for a sweet year?
People then wish each other “a good and sweet year”.
114: How many cups of wine are drunk during the Passover ritual meal?
They recall the 4 expressions of deliverance used in the Exodus story.
115: Who traditionally asks the 4 questions at the start of the Passover meal?
They begin with “Ma nishtanah”: “Why is this night different?”
116: Which minister of the Persian king Ahasuerus wanted to wipe out the Jews of the empire?
During the reading of the story, people make noise every time his name is said.
117: Which holiday marks the end and the new start of the yearly cycle of Torah reading?
People dance while carrying the Torah scrolls.
118: Which Jewish holiday is called the “New Year of the Trees”?
Fruit is traditionally eaten, especially dried fruit.
119: Which fast day commemorates the destruction of both Temples in Jerusalem?
Its name means “the 9th of the month of Av”.
120: Which fruit full of seeds is eaten at the Jewish New Year, with a wish for just as many good deeds?
One tradition says it contains 613 seeds.
121: What is the palm branch waved during Sukkot, the Feast of Tabernacles, called?
It is waved together with 3 other species: the citron, the myrtle and the willow.
122: How many days does the counting of the Omer last, between Passover and Shavuot?
Shavuot falls on the 50th day; its name means “weeks”.
123: Which text, chanted at the start of Yom Kippur, is about cancelling vows?
Its name means “all vows” in Aramaic.
124: What is the minimum number of candles lit to welcome Shabbat?
They are traditionally lit by the woman of the house.
125: What is the braided Shabbat bread called?
2 loaves are placed on the table, recalling the double portion of food received in the desert on the eve of Shabbat.
126: Which meat is forbidden by Jewish dietary laws?
According to the Torah, a permitted mammal must chew the cud and have split hooves.
127: What do we call the religious teacher and guide of a Jewish community?
The word “rabbi” means “my master” in Hebrew.
128: In what form is the Torah read during services?
It is copied entirely by hand by a scribe, on parchment.
129: What is the canopy under which a Jewish couple gets married called?
The canopy symbolises the couple’s future home.
130: What does the groom break at the end of a Jewish wedding ceremony?
This gesture recalls the destruction of the Temple, even in moments of joy.
131: According to Jewish dietary laws, which foods must not be mixed?
This rule comes from the verse: “You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk”.
132: What is the ritual bath of purification in Judaism called?
It must be partly fed by natural water, such as rain or a spring.
133: What is the blessing said over a cup of wine at the start of the Shabbat meal called?
134: What is the minimum number of adults needed to form a minyan, the prayer quorum?
Some prayers can only be said in the presence of a minyan.
135: What are the small leather boxes containing verses, worn on the arm and head during prayer, called?
In English they are also called phylacteries.
136: Which prayer in Aramaic is recited by mourners?
It does not mention death but celebrates the greatness of God.
137: What are Jews whose ancestors lived in Germany and Eastern Europe called?
Ashkenaz was the name for Germany in medieval Hebrew.
138: Which famous Jewish physicist, born in Germany, came up with the theory of relativity?
He received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.
139: Which family of Jewish heroes led a revolt against the Greek kings in the 2nd century BC?
Their victory is the origin of the holiday of Hanukkah.
140: According to a legend from Prague, which clay creature was brought to life to protect the Jews?
The legend credits Rabbi Judah Loew, known as the Maharal, in the 16th century.
141: What is the scattering of Jews around the world, outside the land of Israel, called?
The word comes from Greek and means “scattering”.
142: Which great collection gathers the rabbis’ discussions on Jewish law and tradition?
There are 2 versions: the Jerusalem Talmud and the Babylonian Talmud.
143: Which language, derived from Castilian, was spoken by the Jews expelled from Spain and their descendants?
It was long spoken in Thessaloniki, Istanbul and Tetouan.
144: Which Jewish painter, born in the Russian Empire and famous for his fiddlers and flying lovers, lived in France?
He painted the ceiling of the Palais Garnier opera house in Paris.
145: Which fortress by the Dead Sea was the last stronghold of the great Jewish revolt of the 1st century?
Perched on a rocky plateau, it fell around 73-74 after a long siege.
146: Which king of Judea, in the 1st century BC, had the Second Temple lavishly enlarged?
Work on the esplanade went on for decades after his death.
147: In which Italian city was the first district called a “ghetto” created in 1516?
The word is thought to come from an old foundry (“geto”) located in the district.
148: Near which Dead Sea site were very old biblical manuscripts discovered around 1947?
They are among the oldest known copies of texts from the Hebrew Bible.
149: Which 1st-century Jewish historian wrote about the great Jewish revolt against Rome?
He wrote in Greek, and his work is a major source on this period.
150: According to Genesis, for how many days and nights did the rain of the flood fall?
The waters then covered the earth for 150 days (Genesis 7).
151: According to Genesis, what did one of Isaac’s sons give up to his twin brother for a bowl of lentil stew?
He had come back from the fields exhausted and starving (Genesis 25).
152: According to Genesis, what did God create on the first day?
God separated the light from the darkness and called the light “day” (Genesis 1).
153: According to Genesis, what did God form the first man from?
God then breathed the breath of life into his nostrils (Genesis 2).
154: According to Genesis, what did God compare the number of Abraham’s promised descendants to?
He also compared them to the sand on the seashore (Genesis 15 and 22).
155: What is the Hebrew Bible, made up of the Torah, the Prophets and the Writings, called?
The name is made from the Hebrew initials of its 3 parts: T, N and K.
156: According to Genesis, who was the youngest of Jacob’s sons?
His mother died giving birth to him on the road to Bethlehem (Genesis 35).
157: According to Genesis, what was Abraham’s name before God changed it?
The text explains the new name as “father of a multitude” (Genesis 17).
158: According to Genesis, on which mountains did Noah’s ark come to rest?
The text speaks of the “mountains of Ararat”, a region north of Mesopotamia (Genesis 8).
159: According to Genesis, what did Jacob cover his hands and neck with to pass himself off as his brother to his blind father?
His brother was hairy, while Jacob’s skin was smooth (Genesis 27).
160: According to Genesis, what were the names of Joseph’s 2 sons born in Egypt?
Jacob blessed them with his hands crossed, putting the younger before the elder (Genesis 48).
161: According to Genesis, which figure, the father of Methuselah, “walked with God” and then was no more, because God took him?
Genesis says he lived 365 years on earth (Genesis 5).
162: According to Genesis, which feeling is Isaac’s name linked to?
His parents laughed when they learned they would have a son at a very old age (Genesis 17 and 18).
163: According to the Torah, which animals overran Egypt in the 2nd plague?
They came up out of the Nile and got into houses and even ovens.
164: According to the Torah, which plague plunged Egypt into darkness for 3 days?
The Hebrews, however, had light where they lived (Exodus 10).
165: According to the Torah, which insects devoured Egypt’s crops in the 8th plague?
An east wind brought them and a west wind swept them into the sea (Exodus 10).
166: According to the Torah, what did Moses strike with his staff to make water gush out in the desert?
The place was named Massah and Meribah (Exodus 17).
167: According to the Torah, which animal began to speak to the seer Balaam?
The animal had seen an angel blocking the road before its master did (Numbers 22).
168: According to the Torah, how old was Moses when he died?
The text says his eyesight had not dimmed and his strength was still intact (Deuteronomy 34).
169: According to the Torah, which tribe did Moses come from?
The members of this tribe were put in charge of service in the sanctuary.
170: According to the Torah, why did Moses flee Egypt as an adult?
The Egyptian was beating a Hebrew; Moses then took refuge in the land of Midian (Exodus 2).
171: According to the Torah, on which day of the week did the food from heaven not fall in the desert?
The day before, the Hebrews gathered a double portion (Exodus 16).
172: According to the Torah, what was noticed about Moses’ face when he came down the mountain with the second Tablets?
From then on Moses covered his face with a veil to speak to the people (Exodus 34).
173: According to the Book of Numbers, what did Moses make to heal the Hebrews bitten by snakes?
He put it on a pole: anyone who looked at it was healed (Numbers 21).
174: According to the Torah, which cousin of Moses led a revolt against him and was swallowed up by the earth?
His allies Dathan and Abiram were swallowed up with him (Numbers 16).
175: According to the Torah, which spy sent into Canaan, from the tribe of Judah, declared that the land could be conquered?
Along with one other spy, he was one of the only adults who left Egypt to enter the Promised Land (Numbers 14).
176: In the famous biblical judgment, how did the king find out the real mother of a baby claimed by 2 women?
He proposed cutting the baby in 2
He made them swear an oath
The real mother preferred to give up the child so that it would live (1 Kings 3).
177: According to the Book of Judges, which animal did a hero of immense strength tear apart with his bare hands?
Later he found a swarm of bees and honey in the animal’s carcass (Judges 14).
178: According to the Bible, how many days did the prophet swallowed by a great fish spend in its belly?
The text says 3 days and 3 nights.
179: According to the Bible, what did the prophet Elijah call down from heaven onto his offering on Mount Carmel?
The prophets of Baal had called on their god all day long with no answer (1 Kings 18).
180: According to the Bible, how many stones did the young shepherd pick up from a stream before facing Goliath?
He chose smooth ones and put them in his shepherd’s bag (1 Samuel 17).
181: According to the Bible, which birds brought bread and meat to the prophet Elijah as he hid by a brook?
Elijah had taken refuge by the brook Cherith during a great drought (1 Kings 17).
182: According to the Bible, what was the name of King Solomon’s mother?
She had previously been the wife of Uriah, a soldier in David’s army (2 Samuel 11).
183: According to the Bible, what was the name of King Saul’s son, a close friend of David?
He died in battle against the Philistines, along with his father (1 Samuel 31).
184: According to the Book of Daniel, what were Daniel’s 3 companions thrown into for refusing to worship a golden statue?
They came out without even the smell of fire on them (Daniel 3).
185: According to the Bible, which country did the cedar wood for Solomon’s Temple come from?
King Hiram of Tyre supplied the wood in exchange for wheat and oil (1 Kings 5).
186: According to the Bible, which son of David rebelled against his father and got caught by his head in the branches of an oak tree?
He was famous for his good looks and his thick head of hair (2 Samuel 14 and 18).
187: According to the Bible, which prophet told King David the parable of the poor man’s lamb to rebuke him for his wrongdoing?
In the story, a rich man took a poor man’s only lamb instead of one of his own (2 Samuel 12).
188: Which Jew, cupbearer to the Persian king Artaxerxes, returned to Jerusalem to rebuild its walls?
The book that bears his name says the wall was finished in 52 days.
189: During the Passover meal, what do the bitter herbs recall?
These herbs are called maror; horseradish or lettuce is often used.
190: What do children traditionally receive at Hanukkah?
Chocolate ones are given too; in Yiddish they are called “gelt”.
191: In which season does Passover fall?
It begins on the 15th of the month of Nisan, the first month of the biblical calendar.
192: During which holiday are doughnuts fried in oil, called sufganiyot, traditionally eaten?
Fried potato pancakes, latkes, are also eaten for the same reason.
193: How many days does Rosh Hashanah last?
It lasts 2 days everywhere in the world, even in Jerusalem.
194: What are foods made from leavened grain, forbidden during Passover, called?
Before the holiday, the house is given a big clean to remove every trace of it.
195: In the Purim story, what was the name of the cousin who raised the future queen?
He had foiled a plot against the king, which later earned him great honour.
196: What kind of food is traditionally eaten on Shavuot?
Cheesecakes and cheese-filled pancakes are especially popular.
197: According to the Torah, how many days does Sukkot last?
It is followed by another holiday, Shemini Atzeret (Leviticus 23).
198: What is the piece of matzah hidden during the Passover ritual meal, which children have to find?
It is eaten at the end of the meal, as a kind of “dessert”.
199: Which holiday, on the 33rd day of the counting of the Omer, is often celebrated with bonfires?
Its name comes from Hebrew letters whose total value is 33.
200: What is the mixture of fruit, nuts and wine at the Passover meal, recalling the mortar used by the slaves, called?
Its colour and texture evoke the bricks the Hebrews made in Egypt.
201: Outside the Land of Israel, what sentence do the 4 letters on the Hanukkah spinning top stand for?
In the Land of Israel, one letter changes and the sentence becomes “… happened here”.
202: What is the six-pointed star that is a Jewish symbol called?
In Hebrew it is called Magen David, the “Shield of David”.
203: What does the Hebrew word “shalom”, used as a greeting, mean?
The same word is used to say both hello and goodbye.
204: According to the Torah, which action is explicitly forbidden in every home on Shabbat?
It is one of the few kinds of work the Torah names specifically in connection with Shabbat (Exodus 35).
205: What is traditionally placed on a Jewish grave as a sign of a visit?
Unlike flowers, a stone does not wilt: it stands for a lasting memory.
206: According to Jewish dietary laws, which mammals may be eaten?
The camel, which chews the cud but does not have split hooves, is therefore forbidden (Leviticus 11).
207: How many daily prayer services does Jewish tradition set for weekdays?
208: What is the sacred cabinet in a synagogue, facing the congregation, that holds the Torah called?
In Hebrew it is called Aron ha-Kodesh; it is often covered by a curtain.
209: According to Jewish tradition, how can you tell that Shabbat is over on Saturday evening?
Shabbat therefore lasts a little over 24 hours.
210: What is the circumcision ceremony for a baby boy at 8 days old called?
Its name means “covenant of circumcision”, recalling the covenant with Abraham.
211: What is the prayer book used by Jews every day called?
For the High Holidays, a special book called the machzor is used.
212: What is the small pointer ending in a hand, used to follow the reading of the Torah, called?
This way, the parchment is not touched with the fingers.
213: What is the 7-day mourning period that follows a burial called?
Its name comes from the Hebrew word for 7.
214: Which central prayer, said standing and quietly, is also called “the 18 blessings”?
A 19th blessing was added later, but the traditional name stuck.
215: Which Jewish immigrant born in Bavaria gave his name to a famous brand of jeans?
He founded his company in San Francisco, California, in 1853.
